title: Seven years of filings, one direction
lede: Chi-Chi’s was a division of other companies after 1988, so its own accounts are thin. Its parent reported the division separately from 1996 to 2002, and those seven years are the core of this section. Earlier figures come from the chain’s own history page and a reference history, and are marked.

blocks.title: Restaurants: up in ten years, down in twenty
blocks.subtitle: Restaurants in the system at the dates a source gives a count. The kinds of count differ; see the source line.
blocks.xLabel: Date of the count (not evenly spaced)

points.title: year five
points.text: 92 company-owned and franchised restaurants, from four in the first full year.[^1]

points.title: the third owner
points.text: 235 restaurants operated or franchised when Family Restaurants takes over.[^3]

points.title: reported on its own
points.text: 184 company-operated and 18 franchised or licensed at the end of 1996.[^4]

points.title: the last annual report
points.text: 128 company-operated and 8 franchised or licensed, all 8 of them abroad.[^7]

points.title: closed
points.text: The U.S. restaurants cease operations on September 20, 2004.[^21]

points.title: one again
points.text: A licensed restaurant opens in St. Louis Park, Minnesota.[^36]

blocks.source: 1975–76: the first restaurant.[^1][^2] 92 in “year five”, which we place about 1981.[^1] 200 by 1986, from a reference history.[^2] 235 operated or franchised in January 1994.[^3] 1996 to 2002: company-operated plus franchised and licensed at each year end (184+18, 165+12, 140+13, 128+8).[^4][^5][^7] Zero is the U.S. chain after September 20, 2004; licensed restaurants abroad stayed open and are not counted.[^21][^40]

blocks.title: Chi-Chi’s sales, as its owners reported them
blocks.subtitle: $ millions. The first bar is Foodmaker’s fiscal year to October 3, 1993 (53 weeks); 1994 and 1995 were not reported separately.
blocks.source: FY1993: Foodmaker’s annual report, which consolidated Chi-Chi’s.[^11] 1996 and 1997: Family Restaurants.[^4] 1998 and 1999: Prandium.[^5] 2000 to 2002: Prandium.[^6][^7] Figures are rounded from thousands. Fiscal 2000 had 53 weeks.[^7] From 1996 to 2002 sales fell 33% (derived).

blocks.title: Sales at comparable restaurants
blocks.subtitle: Change on the year before, in percent, as reported in each year’s filing.
blocks.source: Family Restaurants and Prandium annual reports.[^4][^5][^6][^7] In 2002 the fall was $13.1M on a comparable base.[^7]

blocks.title: What the division earned before overheads above it
blocks.subtitle: Chi-Chi’s divisional EBITDA, $ millions. It covers restaurant cash flow less the division’s own administration, before interest, depreciation and the parent’s costs.
blocks.source: Family Restaurants and Prandium annual reports.[^4][^5][^6][^7] Exact figures in thousands: (4,278), 36, 1,426, 5,942, 557, 4,775 and 9,161. The 2002 figure is 4.9% of sales (derived). The filings’ definition excludes interest and depreciation, so this is not profit.

blocks.title: The 1994 deal, as the two sides described it
blocks.subtitle: What Family Restaurants paid for Chi-Chi’s, $ millions.
blocks.source: The total is Family Restaurants’ figure of about $270.0M, “including the assumption of capitalized lease and debt obligations.”[^46] The three parts are Foodmaker’s.[^11] That they add up to the total is our arithmetic (derived), and the two filings differ slightly on the cash; see the data notes. Foodmaker also received a warrant.

blocks.title: What Outback actually bought
blocks.subtitle: The 76 properties in the designation-rights sale, by how Chi-Chi’s held them (shares derived).
blocks.source: Outback Steakhouse, Form 8-K, September 3, 2004.[^18] Shares are derived and rounded to whole squares: 23 of 76 is 30.3% and 15 of 76 is 19.7%. The price works out to about $559,000 a property (derived: $42.5M ÷ 76).

blocks.title: Fifteen people given shots for every one who fell ill
blocks.equation: 9,000 ÷ 601 ≈ 15.0. The 9,000 is the CDC’s approximate figure from November 2003; the 601 is its final count, published in 2005.[^12][^13]

blocks.title: How the count grew
blocks.subtitle: Cases attributed to the Beaver Valley Mall restaurant, by source and date.
blocks.source: Associated Press[^14][^20], CDC[^12][^13] and the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review.[^23] We use the CDC’s published count and note the press figure; see “Conflicts between sources.”
